# knowledge/apis/ — Agent Instructions

`TMFxxx` — TM Forum Open API (OpenAPI/Swagger) schemas, one folder per
API id:

```
knowledge/apis/{TMFxxx}/
├── {TMFxxx}_v{version}.json        the OpenAPI/Swagger schema, unmodified
├── {TMFxxx}_v{version}.meta.json   envelope for that version
└── samples/                        example request/response payloads (optional, best-effort)
```

## Rules specific to APIs

1. **The filename's `v{version}` is load-bearing.** The schema supports
   more than one version of the same API coexisting side by side (a newer
   version doesn't replace an older one already referenced by a use case
   or component) — always match the exact version a `links.apis` entry or
   a component's `dependentAPIs`/`exposedAPIs` list names, don't assume
   "latest" is what's being referenced.
2. **`samples/` is optional and best-effort.** It requires a
   `tmforum-rand`-authorized GitHub token and fails closed (skipped, not
   errored) when unavailable — an API folder with no `samples/` is not a
   bug, and don't fabricate example payloads to fill the gap; read the
   schema's own request/response definitions instead.
3. **`{TMFxxx}.json` is the schema exactly as published** — don't
   "correct" or reformat it. If something in it looks wrong, that's
   either a real upstream issue (report it, don't silently patch the
   cache) or a misreading of the OpenAPI spec on your part.
4. **A `TMFCxxx` (has the `C`) is a Component id, never an API id** — a
   Component's own `component.yaml` *references* API ids like these by
   number (`TMF632`, never `TMFC632`); don't confuse the two when
   resolving a reference found in prose.

## Provenance and regeneration

Generated by `tools/fetch_api.py` (schema) and `tools/fetch_api_samples.py`
(samples) — both automated track, public, safe to schedule
(`spec.md` §5.3/§5.3.1, §6.2). Don't hand-edit any file here; re-run the
fetch script instead, and it will only rewrite what actually changed.
